newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - PowerGen strategy in the spotlight.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - PowerGen strategy in the spotlight.

text.p: First-half results next Thursday from Britain's second biggest electricity generator, PowerGen Plc, could throw some light on how the firm plans to use its financial muscle after its bid for regional power firm Midlands Electricity Plc was blocked this year, analysts said.
The generator is forecast to make pretax profits before exceptional items of between 124 million and 164 million stg, up from 133 million last time.
The dividend is set to rise to about 7.6 pence a share from 6.5 pence.
But investors are more interested in what the company has to say on strategy than the figures, especially since the first half is not the season for heavy electricity demand.

With a healthy balance sheet, strong cash flow and low gearing, analysts are looking for hints on whether the group intends to make acquisitions, hand cash to shareholders -- with another buy-back or a special dividemd -- or both.

The company spent 400 million stg buying back 10 percent of its shares earlier this year. "They were banned from buying Midlands Electricity, the question now is what is plan B," said Nigel Hawkins, utilities analyst at Yamaichi.
"The strategic question is how they will use their balance sheet," said Simon Taylor, utilities analyst at Barclays de Zoete Wedd.
Other issues are how the group's businesses are doing overseas, and what plans PowerGen has for its Kinetica gas business, which has been making losses, analysts said.
The shares have had a strong run, but are still seen as significantly undervalued. BZW's Taylor is recommending them as a "buy".
